key_insight: SwimBird enables a hybrid autoregressive MLLM to dynamically switch between textual chain-of-thought and visual latent "thoughts," preserving strong text reasoning while boosting vision-intensive reasoning through a learned mode switch.
problem_solved: Most MLLMs either rely on text-based chain-of-thought (weak for vision-heavy tasks) or inject fixed visual latent states (which can harm text reasoning); SwimBird resolves this trade-off by making reasoning mode switchable and task-adaptive.
method: Augment a hybrid autoregressive multimodal LLM with a lightweight learned mode switch that selects between textual CoT decoding and injected visual latent states during generation.
Condition the switch on input cues (e.g., task type, prompt signals, or visual features) so the model uses visual "thoughts" only when beneficial while defaulting to textual reasoning otherwise.
Train/finetune with mixed-task objectives and targeted supervision so both modes remain performant and the model learns when to transition smoothly between them.
impact: Provides a practical way to get the best of textual and visual reasoning in one MLLM without sacrificing either capability, making multimodal systems more reliable across both language-centric and vision-intensive tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two decoding branches (Textual CoT vs Visual latent states) with a central learned switch/gate controlling flow
Before/after comparison chart illustrating trade-off: fixed-visual method (improved vision, degraded text) vs SwimBird (balanced performance)

Iconography: toggle/switch, brain (text reasoning) and eye (visual reasoning) to reinforce the switchable modes concept
paper_title: SwimBird: Eliciting Switchable Reasoning Mode in Hybrid Autoregressive MLLMs
paper_authors: Jintao Tong, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Xiaojun Tang, Kunyu Shi
